description: Application metrics, business metrics, SLIs/SLOs, and metrics-driven development for Java applications

questions.question: What is the difference between SLI, SLO, and SLA?
questions.answer: SLI (Service Level Indicator): Quantitative measure of service level. Example: request latency, error rate, throughput. SLO (Service Level Objective): Target value for SLI. Example: 99.9% requests succeed, P99 latency < 500ms. SLA (Service Level Agreement): Contract with consequences if SLOs not met. Example: 99.9% uptime SLA with credit if breached. Relationship: SLI measures, SLO targets, SLA promises. Example Payment API: SLI = actual error rate (0.08%), SLO = error rate < 0.1%, SLA = 99.95% availability with 10% credit if breached. SLIs inform if meeting SLOs, SLOs guide SLA commitments. Best practice: SLO tighter than SLA (buffer), error budget = 100% - SLO (0.1% error budget = 1000 errors per million).
